q1.answer: The approximately 1:1 M:M+2 pattern indicates one bromine atom because 79Br and 81Br occur at nearly equal natural abundance. To support the molecular-ion assignment, identify the highest-mass isotope cluster and check whether lower-mass peaks can be explained as chemically plausible fragment losses; only charged fragments are detected.
rubric: Identifies bromine from the 1:1 M:M+2 pattern.
States that the pair should be part of the highest-mass molecular-ion cluster.
Uses plausible fragment losses or isotope-cluster context as supporting evidence.
q1.explanation: A single chlorine would instead give an approximately 3:1 M:M+2 pair. The pattern identifies the isotope signature, while the spectrum context determines whether the cluster is the intact molecular ion.

rubric: Can explain that the carbonyl oxygen has a double bond and the bridging oxygen has two single bonds.
q2.explanation: Both oxygen atoms then have two bonds and two lone pairs, giving each a formal charge of zero.

rubric: Multiplies each isotope mass by its fractional abundance.
Adds the contributions and reports approximately 10.81 u.
q3.explanation: Average atomic mass is a weighted mean, so the more abundant isotope contributes more strongly to the result.
